mainTopic: The end of the Torah-and-liquids comparison, then the greatness of rain, the sins that hold rain back, and the remedy of תפלה.
overview: The עמוד opens by finishing the story of רבי יהושע and the Caesar's daughter: if handsome scholars had been plain, they would have learned even more. It then gives a second reason Torah is like water, wine and milk: all three spoil only through inattention, and Torah is forgotten only through inattention. Next the גמרא turns to rain. רבי חמא ברבי חנינא and רב אושעיא praise the day of rain, comparing it to creation and saying even ישועה grows on it. רבי תנחום בר חנילאי teaches that rain comes only when ישראל's sins are forgiven, and רבי תנחום בריה דרבי חייא teaches that it is held back when they deserve destruction; each time, זעירי brings a different פסוק for the same idea. A list follows of sins that hold back rain: neglecting תרומות ומעשרות, לשון הרע, עזות פנים, ביטול תורה, and גזל. Along the way there is a side discussion about the brazen person: whether brazenness leads to sin or shows a past sin, and whether he may be called a רשע or even hated. רבי אמי teaches that the remedy is strong תפלה for mercy. The עמוד ends as ריש לקיש begins reading the 'blunt iron' פסוק as being about a תלמיד, which continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Had they been ugly, they would have learned more
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע finishes his answer: if the Sages were ugly, they would be even more learned.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they had been ugly, they would have been even more learned.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes רבי יהושע's reply in the story that came right before it. He says that good looks do not help Torah learning; if anything, being plain helps it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the story just before, רבי יהושע compared Torah to wine, which keeps best in plain clay vessels, not in fine ones. The Caesar's daughter objected that some handsome people are learned. He answers that if they had been plain, they would have learned even more.

phrases.english: If they had been ugly —
phrases.notes: "They" means the Torah scholars. This finishes רבי יהושע's answer to the Caesar's daughter.

phrases.english: they would have been even more learned.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הֲווֹ סְנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the aggadic exchange that began earlier on the daf.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Caesar's daughter's objection that some handsome people are also learned in Torah.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Beauty does not help Torah learning. Plainer scholars would have learned even more.

steps.title: A second reason Torah is like water, wine and milk
steps.stepSummary: Just as these three liquids spoil only when no one pays attention to them, Torah is forgotten only when a person stops paying attention.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: just as these three liquids become spoiled only through lack of attention, so too Torah is forgotten only through lack of attention.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different reason why Torah is compared to water, wine and milk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If you guard these liquids, they stay good. They spoil only when you stop watching them. Torah works the same way: it slips away only when a person stops focusing on it.

keyTerms.meaning: taking one's mind off something, inattention

steps.whatToRemember: Torah is not lost by accident. It is forgotten only when a person stops paying attention to it.

phrases.english: Another explanation:
just as these three liquids
phrases.notes: Water, wine and milk, the three liquids Torah was compared to earlier.

phrases.english: become spoiled only through lack of attention —
so too, words of Torah are forgotten
only through lack of attention.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different explanation of the same comparison of Torah to the three liquids.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Torah is forgotten only through inattention, just as water, wine and milk spoil only through inattention.

steps.title: The day of rain is as great as the day of creation
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא says the day of rain is as great as the day heaven and earth were created, and he brings a פסוק from ישעיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא said: The day of rain is as great as the day heaven and earth were created, as the פסוק says: "Drop down, heavens, from above, and let the skies pour down righteousness; let the earth open and let them bear salvation, and let it cause righteousness to sprout together; I, ה׳, have created it."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to its main topic, rain. רבי חמא ברבי חנינא praises the day of rain and quotes a פסוק to support his point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes rain coming down from the heavens and the earth opening up to grow things. It ends with "I created it," which ties rain to the act of creation. The next step explains exactly how he reads that ending.

keyTerms.meaning: drop down, let fall like drops
let them pour down, let them flow

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥama, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, said:
The day of rain is great
like the day on which heaven and earth were created,
as it says: "Drop down, heavens, from above,
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 45:8

phrases.english: and let the skies pour down righteousness;
let the earth open, and let them bear salvation,
and let it cause righteousness to sprout together;
I, ה׳, have created it."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חָמָא בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא גָּדוֹל יוֹם הַגְּשָׁמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the Torah discussion and returns to the topic of rain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The day of rain is as great as the day heaven and earth were created.

steps.title: "Created it," not "created them"
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק uses the singular "it," so it refers to the rain, which puts rain on the level of creation.
steps.simpleTranslation: It does not say "I created them," but rather "I created it."
steps.whatsHappening: This is the exact proof from the פסוק. The word is singular, "it" (בראתיו), not plural, "them" (בראתים).
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק meant heaven and earth, it would say "them." Since it says "it," the creation is about the rain. Rain is described with the language of creating, so the day of rain is as great as the day of creation.
steps.confusionAlert: The proof rests entirely on one letter: the singular "it" versus the plural "them." Do not look for a bigger argument here.

phrases.english: It does not say "I created them,"
but rather "I created it."

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּרָאתִים לֹא נֶאֱמַר אֶלָּא בְּרָאתִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the פסוק quoted in step 3 proves רבי חמא's claim.
steps.raayaObject: That the day of rain is equal to the day of creation.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The singular word בראתיו at the end of ישעיהו 45:8.

steps.title: Even salvation grows on a day of rain
steps.stepSummary: רב אושעיא says the day of rain is so great that even ישועה multiplies on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אושעיא said: The day of rain is great, since even salvation is fruitful and multiplies on it, as it says: "Let the earth open, and let them bear salvation."
steps.whatsHappening: רב אושעיא gives another praise of the day of rain, using a different phrase from the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק places "salvation" right next to the earth opening up after rain. רב אושעיא learns from this that rain does more than make crops grow. On a day of rain, salvation itself grows in the world.

phrases.english: Rav Oshaya said:
The day of rain is great,
for even salvation is fruitful and multiplies on it,
as it says: "Let the earth open, and let them bear salvation."
phrases.notes: The same פסוק as before, ישעיהו 45:8.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אוֹשַׁעְיָא גָּדוֹל יוֹם הַגְּשָׁמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second praise of the day of rain from the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On a day of rain, even salvation grows and multiplies.

steps.title: Rain falls only after sins are forgiven
steps.stepSummary: רבי תנחום בר חנילאי says rain comes only when ישראל's sins have been forgiven, based on a פסוק in תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי תנחום בר חנילאי said: Rain falls only if the sins of ישראל have been forgiven, as it says: "ה׳, You favored Your land; You returned the captivity of יעקב. You forgave the sin of Your people; You covered all their sins, Selah."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי תנחום teaches a new idea: rain is a sign that ישראל's sins have been forgiven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links ה׳ favoring "Your land" with forgiving the people's sins. The land being favored means it gets rain. So rain comes only after forgiveness.

keyTerms.meaning: You favored, You were pleased with

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a spiritual reason for the whole topic of praying and fasting for rain: when rain is held back, the need is for forgiveness.

phrases.english: Rabbi Tanḥum bar Ḥanilai said:
Rain does not fall

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן נִמְחֲלוּ עֲוֹנוֹתֵיהֶן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: unless the sins of Israel have been forgiven,
as it says: "ה׳, You favored Your land;
phrases.notes: תהלים 85:2–3

phrases.english: You returned the captivity of Yaakov.
You forgave the sin of Your people;
You covered all their sins, Selah."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי תַּנְחוּם בַּר חֲנִילַאי אֵין הַגְּשָׁמִים יוֹרְדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of teachings about rain with a new idea: rain depends on forgiveness.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rain falls only when ישראל's sins have been forgiven.

steps.title: A different פסוק for the same idea
steps.stepSummary: זעירי מדיהבת tells רבינא that his community learned רבי תנחום's idea from a different פסוק, in שלמה's prayer.
steps.simpleTranslation: זעירי from Dihavat said to רבינא: You learn it from here; we learn it from here: "Then You hear in heaven, and forgive the sin..."
steps.whatsHappening: זעירי agrees with the idea that rain depends on forgiveness, but he brings a different source for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea itself does not change. Only the source changes. In שלמה's prayer, forgiveness ("and forgive the sin") comes right before the request for rain on the land.

keyTerms.meaning: we learn it, we teach it

steps.whatToRemember: Rain comes only when sins are forgiven. Two different פסוקים teach this: one from תהלים and one from שלמה's prayer.

phrases.english: Ze'iri from Dihavat said to Ravina:
You learn it from here.
We learn it from here:
"Then You hear in heaven,
phrases.notes: מלכים א 8:36, from שלמה's prayer. The rest of that פסוק asks for rain on the land.

phrases.english: and forgive the sin, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתּוּן מֵהָכָא מַתְנִיתוּ לַהּ אֲנַן מֵהָכָא מַתְנֵינַן לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different source for the same teaching as step 6.
steps.raayaObject: That rain depends on the forgiveness of ישראל's sins.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שלמה's prayer in מלכים א 8:36: "Then You hear in heaven and forgive the sin," which is followed by the request for rain.

steps.title: Rain is held back only when ישראל deserve destruction
steps.stepSummary: רבי תנחום בריה דרבי חייא says rain stops only when ישראל have become liable to destruction, based on a פסוק in איוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי תנחום בריה דרבי חייא, from כפר עכו, said: The rains are held back only if the enemies of ישראל (a polite way of saying ישראל) have been sentenced to destruction. As it says: 'Drought and heat steal the snow waters; to the grave, those who sinned.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא gives the reverse side of the earlier idea. Earlier we heard that rain comes when sins are forgiven; now we hear that rain stops when sins are very serious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links two things: the snow waters being 'stolen' by drought, and sinners heading 'to the grave.' רבי תנחום reads this as cause and effect. When ישראל's sins reach the level of deserving destruction, the rain disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: literally 'the enemies of ישראל'; a polite way to avoid saying something bad about ישראל directly

steps.confusionAlert: 'The enemies of ישראל' does not mean actual enemies. The גמרא is speaking politely and means ישראל themselves.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי תַּנְחוּם בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא
phrases.english: Rabbi Tanchum, son of Rabbi Chiyya, said
a man of the village of Akko:
The rains are not held back
unless they have become liable
the enemies of ישראל, to destruction,
phrases.notes: A polite way of saying ישראל themselves, so the text doesn't say something bad about them directly.

phrases.english: as it says:
"Drought and heat steal the snow waters,"
phrases.notes: איוב 24:19

phrases.english: "to the grave, those who sinned."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי תַּנְחוּם בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא אִישׁ כְּפַר עַכּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 6: there, rain comes when sins are forgiven; here, rain stops when sins deserve destruction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rain is withheld only when ישראל have become liable to destruction.

steps.title: זעירי gives a different source from the תורה
steps.stepSummary: זעירי מדיהבת tells רבינא that his community learns רבי תנחום's idea from a פסוק in דברים.
steps.simpleTranslation: זעירי from Dihavat said to רבינא: You learn this idea from here (איוב). We learn it from here: 'And He will close up the heavens... and you will perish quickly.'
steps.whatsHappening: זעירי agrees with the idea but brings a different source for it, a פסוק from the תורה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In דברים, 'closing the heavens' (no rain) appears right next to 'you will perish quickly.' This ties rain stopping directly to ישראל being liable to destruction, which is exactly רבי תנחום's point. This follows the same pattern as step 7, where זעירי offered a different source for the earlier statement.

keyTerms.meaning: זעירי from the town of Dihavat
and He will close up / hold back

phrases.english: זעירי from Dihavat said to רבינא:
You learn it from here (the פסוק in איוב).
We learn it from here:
"And He will close up the heavens"
"and you will perish quickly."
phrases.notes: דברים 11:17. The rain stopping and perishing appear together in one פסוק.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתּוּן, מֵהָכָא מַתְנִיתוּ לַהּ. אֲנַן, מֵהָכָא מַתְנֵינַן לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternate פסוק as the source for step 8's idea.
steps.raayaObject: רבי תנחום's claim that rain is withheld when ישראל deserve destruction.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 11:17: 'And He will close up the heavens... and you will perish quickly.'

steps.title: Rain stops because people neglect תרומות ומעשרות
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says rain is held back only because people stop giving תרומות ומעשרות, using the same פסוק from איוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: The rains are held back only because of the neglect of תרומות ומעשרות. As it says: 'Drought and heat steal the snow waters.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא names one specific sin that causes rain to stop. He quotes the same פסוק רבי תנחום used, but reads it differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is not yet clear how this פסוק has anything to do with תרומות ומעשרות. That gap is what the גמרא asks about in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: the gifts from produce given to the כהן and לוי

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: אֵין הַגְּשָׁמִים נֶעֱצָרִין
phrases.english: רב חסדא said: The rains are not held back
except because of the neglect of תרומות and מעשרות,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״צִיָּה גַם חֹם יִגְזְלוּ מֵימֵי שֶׁלֶג״.
phrases.english: as it says: "Drought and heat steal the snow waters."
phrases.notes: Same פסוק as before (איוב 24:19), now read in a new way.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: אֵין הַגְּשָׁמִים נֶעֱצָרִין אֶלָּא בִּשְׁבִיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a list of specific sins that cause rain to be withheld; uses the same פסוק as step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Neglecting תרומות ומעשרות causes the rain to be withheld.

steps.title: How does the פסוק show this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where in the פסוק we see anything about תרומות ומעשרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where in the פסוק is this understood?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רב חסדא gets תרומות ומעשרות out of the פסוק. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק talks about drought, heat and snow, with no mention of תרומות ומעשרות. The גמרא wants to see the actual link in the words.

keyTerms.meaning: what shows this? how is this implied?

phrases.english: What shows this?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי מַשְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the explanation of רב חסדא's proof.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the פסוק about drought and heat connects to neglecting תרומות ומעשרות.

steps.title: Summer duties neglected, winter rain taken away
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא from the school of רבי ישמעאל explains: 'חם' means summer, when tithes are taken, and 'snow waters' means the winter rains that are lost.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: Because of things I commanded you to do in the summer and you did not do them, the snow waters will be taken from you in the rainy season.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with a teaching from the school of רבי ישמעאל that reads the פסוק as summer and winter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'חם' (heat) is read as the hot season, when produce is harvested and תרומות ומעשרות must be separated. If those duties are skipped in the summer, the 'snow waters' of winter are 'stolen.' This is measure for measure: you held back what you owed, so the rain is held back from you.

keyTerms.meaning: it was taught in the school of רבי ישמעאל

phrases.english: It was taught in the school of רבי ישמעאל:
Because of things that I commanded you
in the summer days, and you did not do them —
phrases.notes: The word 'חם' (heat) in the פסוק is being read as 'summer,' harvest time, when tithes are due.

phrases.english: the snow waters will be taken from you
in the rainy season.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 11's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Heat' means summer, when תרומות ומעשרות are due. Neglecting them causes the winter rain to be 'stolen.'

steps.title: Rain stops because of לשון הרע
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן פזי says rain is held back only because of people who speak לשון הרע, based on a פסוק in משלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן פזי said: The rains are held back only because of those who speak לשון הרע. As it says: 'The north wind brings forth rain, and an angry face, a secret tongue.'
steps.whatsHappening: Another אמורא names a different sin that causes rain to stop: speaking לשון הרע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק places rain next to an 'angry face' and a 'secret tongue,' meaning hidden, harmful talk. רבי שמעון בן פזי reads it this way: when people speak לשון הרע, the heavens show an angry face and the rain is held back.

keyTerms.meaning: those who speak harmful talk about others

phrases.english: רבי שמעון בן פזי said:
The rains are not held back
except because of those who speak לשון הרע,
as it says: "The north wind brings forth rain,"
"and an angry face, a secret tongue."
phrases.notes: משלי 25:23

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן פַּזִּי: אֵין הַגְּשָׁמִים נֶעֱצָרִין אֶלָּא בִּשְׁבִיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another specific sin to the list started by רב חסדא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Speaking לשון הרע causes the rain to be withheld.

steps.title: Rain stops because of brazen people
steps.stepSummary: רב סלא in the name of רב המנונא says rain is held back only because of brazen, shameless people, based on a פסוק in ירמיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב סלא said in the name of רב המנונא: The rains are held back only because of brazen people. As it says: 'The showers were held back and there was no late rain, yet you had the forehead of a harlot...'
steps.whatsHappening: A third sin is added to the list: עזות פנים, being brazen and shameless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the same פסוק, ירמיהו says the rains were held back and also describes the people as having a 'harlot's forehead,' meaning they felt no shame. רב המנונא reads this as cause and effect: shamelessness is why the rain stopped.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב סַלָּא אָמַר רַב הַמְנוּנָא:
phrases.english: רב סלא said in the name of רב המנונא:
The rains are not held back
except because of brazen people,
as it says: "The showers were held back, and there was no late rain,"

phrases.aramaic: וּמֵצַח אִשָּׁה זוֹנָה הָיָה לָךְ וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: "yet you had the forehead of a harlot, etc."
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 3:3. A 'harlot's forehead' means a face that shows no shame.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב סַלָּא אָמַר רַב הַמְנוּנָא: אֵין הַגְּשָׁמִים נֶעֱצָרִין אֶלָּא בִּשְׁבִיל עַזֵּי פָנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third specific sin to the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Brazenness causes the rain to be withheld.

steps.title: A brazen person will end up sinning
steps.stepSummary: Using the same פסוק, רב סלא in the name of רב המנונא adds that anyone brazen will eventually stumble in sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב סלא said in the name of רב המנונא: Any person who is brazen will in the end stumble in sin. As it says: 'You had the forehead of a harlot.'
steps.whatsHappening: The same teacher learns a second lesson from the same פסוק. This one is not about rain but about where shamelessness leads.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links a brazen 'forehead' to a 'harlot.' רב המנונא learns that shamelessness is a path that will lead a person to stumble in sin. Here the sin follows after the brazenness.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב סַלָּא אָמַר רַב הַמְנוּנָא:
phrases.english: And רב סלא said in the name of רב המנונא:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל אָדָם שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ עַזּוּת פָּנִים —
phrases.english: Any person who has brazenness —
will in the end stumble in sin,
as it says: "Yet you had the forehead of a harlot."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב סַלָּא אָמַר רַב הַמְנוּנָא: כׇּל אָדָם שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ עַזּוּת פָּנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching from the same speakers on the same פסוק as step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A brazen person will eventually stumble in sin.

steps.title: רב נחמן: the brazen person has already sinned
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן reads the פסוק differently: brazenness is a sign the person has already sinned, because the פסוק says 'you had,' not 'you will have.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: It is known that he has already stumbled in sin, as it says 'you had,' and it does not say 'you will have.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן disagrees with how רב המנונא reads the פסוק. He says brazenness does not lead to future sin; it shows the sin already happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument rests on the grammar of the פסוק. 'היה לך' is past tense. If the פסוק meant a future result, it would say 'יהיה לך.' So for רב נחמן, shamelessness is the result of a past sin, not a warning about a future one.

keyTerms.meaning: it is known, it is certain

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא lists causes of rain being held back: ישראל being liable to destruction, neglecting תרומות ומעשרות, לשון הרע, and עזות פנים. On עזות פנים, רב המנונא says it leads to future sin, while רב נחמן says it shows a sin already done, based on the past tense 'היה לך.'

phrases.english: רב נחמן said:
It is known that he has already stumbled in sin,
as it says: "you had,"
and it does not say "you will have."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר: בְּיָדוּעַ שֶׁנִּכְשַׁל בַּעֲבֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a competing reading of the same פסוק used in step 15, based on its past tense.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Brazenness is a sign that the person has already sinned.

steps.title: A brazen person may be called wicked
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא rules that it is permitted to call a person with עזות פנים a רשע, based on a פסוק in משלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא said: Anyone who is brazen may be called wicked, because the פסוק says, 'A wicked man makes his face brazen.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps going with the topic of brazen people. רבה בר רב הונא adds a practical rule: you may call such a person a רשע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 15 and 16 linked brazenness to sin. Here רבה בר רב הונא draws a practical result from that link. Because the פסוק puts 'brazen face' and 'wicked man' together, it is permitted to call a brazen person a רשע.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל אָדָם שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ עַזּוּת פָּנִים
phrases.english: Any person who has brazenness of face
it is permitted to call him wicked,
as it says: "A wicked man makes his face brazen."
phrases.notes: משלי 21:29

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא: כׇּל אָדָם שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ עַזּוּת פָּנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of statements about brazen people and adds a practical permission.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It is permitted to call a brazen person a רשע.

steps.title: A brazen person may even be hated
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק goes further and says it is permitted to hate a brazen person. He rereads a word in a פסוק from קהלת as 'hated' instead of 'changed.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: It is permitted to hate him, because the פסוק says 'the brazenness of his face is changed.' Don't read 'changed' (ישנא); read 'hated' (ישנא).
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives a stronger rule than the previous step: you may hate a brazen person. He uses an אל תקרי, a 'don't read it this way, read it that way' reading of a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Hebrew, the words for 'is changed' and 'is hated' are spelled with the same letters. Only the vowels are different. By reading the second meaning into the פסוק, רב נחמן בר יצחק learns that the brazen person's face 'is hated,' so hating him is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Do not read' a method that reads the same letters with different vowels to learn a lesson
'Is changed' versus 'is hated', the same letters with different vowels

steps.confusionAlert: An אל תקרי does not mean the text of the פסוק is wrong. The plain meaning stays. The גמרא is adding a second lesson from how the letters could also be read.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
It is permitted to hate him,
as it says: "And the brazenness of his face is changed."
phrases.notes: קהלת 8:1

phrases.english: Do not read it as "is changed,"
but rather as "is hated."
phrases.notes: Same letters in the Hebrew, just different vowels.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר: מוּתָּר לִשְׂנאוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a stronger permission than רבה בר רב הונא, using a different פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It is permitted to hate a brazen person.

steps.title: Rain is held back because of neglect of Torah
steps.stepSummary: רב קטינא says rain is held back only because of ביטול תורה. He reads a פסוק in קהלת as describing ישראל's laziness in learning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב קטינא said: Rain is held back only because of neglecting תורה, as the פסוק says, 'Through laziness the rafters sink.' Because Israel was lazy and did not learn תורה‎, ה׳ (said politely as 'the enemy of ה׳') became 'poor.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to its list of sins that hold back rain. רב קטינא gives his answer: neglect of תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב קטינא reads 'laziness' as laziness in learning תורה. He reads 'the rafters sink' as ה׳ becoming 'poor,' meaning He holds back His blessing of rain. The next step will prove what the words מך and מקרה mean.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The enemy of ה׳', a respectful way of referring to ה׳ Himself

steps.confusionAlert: 'The enemy of ה׳' does not mean an actual enemy. Out of respect, the גמרא avoids saying directly that ה׳ became poor.

phrases.english: Rav Ketina said:
The rains are not held back
except because of neglect of Torah,
as it says: "Through laziness the rafters sink."
phrases.notes: קהלת 10:18

phrases.english: Because of laziness that was among Israel
that they did not busy themselves with Torah,

phrases.aramaic: נַעֲשֶׂה שׂוֹנְאוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מָךְ.
phrases.english: the "enemy of the Holy One, Blessed be He" became poor.
phrases.notes: He really means ה׳ Himself. The גמרא just says it politely.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב קַטִּינָא: אֵין הַגְּשָׁמִים נֶעֱצָרִין אֶלָּא בִּשְׁבִיל בִּיטּוּל תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the side discussion about brazenness, returns to the list of sins that hold back rain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rain is held back because of ביטול תורה.

steps.title: Proving what 'sink' and 'rafters' mean
steps.stepSummary: רב קטינא proves from other פסוקים that מך means 'poor' and that מקרה refers to ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'מך' means poor, as in 'if he is too poor for your valuation.' 'מקרה' means ה׳, as in 'Who lays the beams of His upper chambers in the water.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב קטינא backs up his reading. He shows from other פסוקים that the two key words really carry the meanings he gave them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His reading needed two links: 'sink' must mean 'poor,' and 'rafters' must mean ה׳. Each link is proven from a פסוק where the same word clearly has that meaning. In ויקרא, מך means a poor person. In תהלים, המקרה describes ה׳ building His heavenly chambers.

keyTerms.meaning: Rafters / one who lays beams, here referring to ה׳
'X means nothing other than Y', a formula for defining a word

phrases.english: And "sink" (מך) means nothing other than poor,
as it says: "And if he is too poor for your valuation."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:8

phrases.english: And "rafters" (מקרה) means nothing other than the Holy One, Blessed be He,
as it says: "Who lays the beams of His upper chambers in the water."
phrases.notes: תהלים 104:3

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין ״מָךְ״ אֶלָּא עָנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the word meanings that רב קטינא's reading depends on.
steps.raayaObject: That מך means poor and מקרה refers to ה׳.

steps.title: Another source for neglect of Torah holding back rain
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף proves the same idea from a פסוק in איוב. 'Light' means תורה, so when people do not see the 'light,' the sky stays clear of rain clouds.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: We learn it from here: 'And now they did not see light; it is bright in the skies, and a wind passed and cleared them.' 'Light' means תורה, as it says, 'For a מצוה is a lamp and תורה is light.' So, without תורה, 'it is bright in the skies' and there are no rain clouds.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף agrees that neglect of תורה holds back rain, but he brings a different פסוק as the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key move is reading 'light' as תורה, proven from משלי. Then the פסוק reads: when people do not see תורה, the sky is 'bright,' meaning clear with no clouds, so no rain falls.

keyTerms.meaning: From here, introducing a different source for the same idea

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: From here:
"And now they did not see light;
it is bright in the skies,
and a wind passed and cleared them."
phrases.notes: איוב 37:21

phrases.english: And "light" means nothing other than Torah,
as it says: "For a מצוה is a lamp and Torah is light."
phrases.notes: משלי 6:23

phrases.english: So "it is bright in the skies."
phrases.notes: When people don't 'see' תורה, the sky stays clear, with no rain clouds.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר, מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different פסוק for רב קטינא's idea that ביטול תורה holds back rain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rain is held back because of ביטול תורה, learned from איוב 37:21.

steps.title: Even full rain clouds get blown away
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא from the school of רבי ישמעאל explains the end of רב יוסף's פסוק. Even when the sky is full of rain-ready clouds, a wind comes and clears them away.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: Even when the sky fills with bright clouds ready to bring down dew and rain, 'a wind passed and cleared them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that explains the last part of the פסוק רב יוסף quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף explained 'it is bright in the skies' as a sky with no clouds. The ברייתא adds a further point: even if rain clouds do form, a wind blows them away. Either way, no rain falls when תורה is neglected.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in the school of רבי ישמעאל
Bright clouds that are ready to give rain

steps.whatToRemember: Two sources (רב קטינא and רב יוסף) agree that neglect of תורה holds back rain. The ברייתא adds that even clouds full of rain can be blown away.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
Even at a time when the sky becomes
full of bright clouds
phrases.notes: Literally 'bright ones, bright ones,' meaning clouds ready with rain.

phrases.english: to bring down dew and rain,
"a wind passed and cleared them."

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: אֲפִילּוּ בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁרָקִיעַ נַעֲשֶׂה בְּהוֹרִין בְּהוֹרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the end of the פסוק from איוב that רב יוסף quoted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even when rain clouds form, they are blown away if תורה is neglected.

steps.title: Rain is held back because of robbery
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי says rain is held back only because of the sin of גזל. He reads 'over the hands He covered light' as 'because of the sin of the hands, ה׳ covered the light.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: Rain is held back only because of the sin of robbery, as the פסוק says, 'Over the hands He covered light.' This means: because of the sin of the hands, He covered the light.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another opinion to the list of sins that hold back rain. רבי אמי says it is robbery.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי reads 'על כפים' as 'because of what the hands did.' He reads 'covered light' as ה׳ holding back something good. The next step proves that 'hands' means robbery and 'light' means rain.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין הַגְּשָׁמִים נֶעֱצָרִין אֶלָּא בַּעֲוֹן גָּזֵל,
phrases.english: The rains are held back only because of the sin of robbery,
as it says: "Over the hands He covered light."
phrases.notes: איוב 36:32

phrases.english: Because of the sin of the hands,
He covered the light.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי: אֵין הַגְּשָׁמִים נֶעֱצָרִין אֶלָּא בַּעֲוֹן גָּזֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Names a different sin, robbery, as the cause of rain being held back.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rain is held back because of גזל.

steps.title: Proving what 'hands' and 'light' mean
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי proves that כפים refers to robbery (חמס) and that אור here means rain, using פסוקים from יונה and איוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Hands' means robbery, as it says, 'and from the robbery that is in their hands.' 'Light' means rain, as it says, 'He spreads the cloud of His light.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי backs up his reading by proving the meaning of the two key words from other פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In יונה, the people of נינוה repent from 'the robbery in their hands,' which links hands to robbery. In איוב, 'the cloud of His light' links light to clouds and rain. Earlier, רב יוסף read אור as תורה. Here רבי אמי reads the same word as rain, in a different פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He spreads the cloud of His light'

steps.whatToRemember: The list of sins that hold back rain now includes לשון הרע, brazenness, neglect of תורה, and robbery.

phrases.english: And "hands" means nothing other than robbery,
as it says: "And from the robbery that is in their hands."
phrases.notes: יונה 3:8

phrases.english: And "light" means nothing other than rain,
as it says: "He spreads the cloud of His light."
phrases.notes: איוב 37:11

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין ״כַּפַּיִם״ אֶלָּא חָמָס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the word meanings that רבי אמי's reading depends on.
steps.raayaObject: That כפים refers to robbery and אור refers to rain.

steps.title: The remedy for rain held back by robbery is more prayer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what a person whose גזל held back the rain can do. The answer is to increase תפלה. This is proven from a פסוק in איוב, since the word פגיעה means prayer, as shown in ירמיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is his fix? He should pray more. The פסוק says 'He commanded it through imploring,' and 'imploring' (פגיעה) always means prayer, as we see in ירמיה: 'Do not pray for this nation... and do not implore Me.'
steps.whatsHappening: After saying that rain stops because of גזל, the גמרא now gives the way to fix it: pray more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof works in two links. First, the פסוק in איוב (from the same section about rain) says ה׳ 'commands' the rain because of מפגיע. Second, ירמיה uses תפגע right next to תתפלל, which shows that פגיעה means תפלה.

keyTerms.meaning: His remedy, his way to fix it
Imploring, begging; here it means prayer

steps.whyThisMatters: It turns a frightening statement (rain is withheld because of sin) into a practical message: תפלה can bring the rain back.

phrases.english: What is his remedy?
phrases.notes: He means the person whose robbery caused the rain to be held back.

phrases.english: He should increase in prayer,
as it is said: "And He commanded it through imploring,"
phrases.notes: איוב 36:32

phrases.english: and "imploring" means nothing other than prayer,
as it is said: "And you, do not pray
for this nation, etc.
and do not implore Me."
phrases.notes: ירמיה 7:16

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי תַּקַּנְתֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי אמי's teaching about גזל by giving the remedy.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One whose sin held back the rain should increase his תפלה.

steps.title: A sky hard as iron comes from a corrupt generation
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי explains the פסוק in קהלת 'If the iron is blunt.' If the sky is 'hard as iron' and gives no טל ומטר, it is because the deeds of the generation are corrupt, read from the word קלקל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: what does 'If the iron is blunt and he does not sharpen the edge' mean? If you see the sky hard like iron, not letting down dew and rain, it is because the generation's deeds are corrupt, as the פסוק says 'קלקל.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי gives a second teaching about rain, reading a פסוק in קהלת as talking about a sky that will not give rain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads 'blunt iron' as a sky that is closed and hard like metal. He reads the word קלקל as connected to מקולקלין, 'corrupt,' so the second half of the פסוק gives the reason: the generation's bad deeds.

keyTerms.meaning: Blunt, dull; here, hard and closed

phrases.english: And Rabbi Ami said:
What is meant by what is written:
"If the iron is blunt,
and he does not sharpen the edge"?
phrases.notes: קהלת 10:10

phrases.english: If you see a sky
that is hard like iron
so it does not bring down dew and rain,
it is because of the deeds of the generation
which are corrupt,
as it is said: "and he does not sharpen the edge."
phrases.notes: He hears the word קלקל as connected to מקולקלין, "corrupt."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי, מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching by the same רבי אמי on the same theme: sin holds back rain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the sky gives no rain, it is because of the generation's corrupt deeds.

steps.title: The remedy is to pray hard for mercy
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי continues: the remedy for the generation is to pray strongly for רחמים, from the next words of the same פסוק. If their deeds had been proper from the start, all the more so the rain would have come.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is their fix? They should pray strongly for mercy, as the פסוק says 'he must increase strength.' And 'wisdom's advantage is in making things right' means: how much better if their deeds had been proper from the beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי reads the rest of the קהלת פסוק to give the fix: pray hard for mercy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Increase strength' is read as putting more strength into prayers for רחמים. The last words, הכשיר חכמה, teach a כל שכן: prayer helps after the damage, but proper deeds from the start would have been even better.

keyTerms.meaning: They should strengthen themselves in prayers for mercy

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אמי's two teachings follow the same pattern: sin holds back rain, and strong תפלה is the remedy. Best of all is to act properly from the start.

phrases.english: What is their remedy?
They should strengthen themselves in prayers for mercy,
as it is said: "Then he must increase strength,
and wisdom's advantage is in making things right."
phrases.notes: These are the next words of the same פסוק, קהלת 10:10.

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן אִם הוּכְשְׁרוּ מַעֲשֵׂיהֶן מֵעִיקָּרָא.
phrases.english: All the more so if their deeds had been made right from the beginning.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה תַּקָּנָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבי אמי's reading of the פסוק by giving the remedy.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The generation should pray strongly for mercy; proper deeds from the start would have been even better.

steps.title: ריש לקיש begins a different reading of the same verse
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש starts his own explanation of the 'blunt iron' פסוק, about a תלמיד. His statement continues on the next עמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: If you see a student...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line: ריש לקיש begins a new way to read the same פסוק, and the rest comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי read the 'iron' as the sky; ריש לקיש is about to read it as a תלמיד. The same פסוק is now being applied to Torah learning instead of rain.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
If you see a student
phrases.notes: He's reading the same "blunt iron" פסוק; his words continue on the next עמוד.

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: אִם רָאִיתָ תַּלְמִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different interpretation of the פסוק that רבי אמי just explained.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Opening of ריש לקיש's reading of the פסוק as being about a תלמיד (continues on the next part of the daf).
